facts.material: polypropylene upper rake panel and lower scoop panel (majority of weight and bulk), aluminum handle and pole, steel fasteners and hardware
facts.function: rakes, gathers, grips, lifts and transports yard debris
facts.form: complete long-handled rake/scoop, about 60 in long

gri_path: Chapter 82 note 1: hand tools of chapter 82 must have a blade, working edge or working surface of base metal; the working rake and scoop panels are plastic, so heading 8201 is excluded
GRI 3(b): composite of plastic and aluminum; the polypropylene panels give essential character (majority of weight and bulk, perform the raking and scooping function)
GRI 1: among plastic headings, 3924 other household articles of plastics covers a yard rake used around the household (as with plastic rake hands in N333477) over residual 3926

rejected_alternatives.reason: chapter 82 note 1 requires a working part of base metal; the rake working parts are plastic
aluminum handle/pole does not give essential character (plastic is majority of weight and bulk and performs the function)
residual plastics heading; 3924 covers household articles and CBP treats household yard-debris rakes as such

classification.rationale: The rake cannot be a chapter 82 hand tool because its working surfaces are plastic, not base metal (chapter 82 note 1). As a composite of plastic panels and an aluminum pole, the polypropylene gives essential character under GRI 3(b), as stated in the facts. CBP classified plastic rake hands for scooping leaves and yard debris as household articles of plastics in 3924.90.5650 (NY N333477, in force), and this household yard rake follows that line.
